findings.finding: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For huge M=3^{2025!}, n=M+δ (δ≪M). Minimal L=⌈n/2⌉ works (a,b proper divisors of L exist), so f(n)=⌈n/2⌉≈M/2. Then g(c)=⌊2025!·L/M⌋/2025!=½. All six terms give ½ ⇒ sum=3=3/1 ⇒ p+q=4. Answer 4.

Key: f(n)=min L≥⌈n/2⌉ with distinct proper divisors a,b of L, a+b=n−L. For n=M (M=3^{2025!}) L=2M works: a=3^{K−1},b=2·3^{K−1},c=2·3^{K} sum M. Thus f(M)=2M. For n=M+δ (δ≪M) L=⌈(M+δ)/2⌉ works (a,b from powers of 3 and 2·powers). Hence g(c)=½ for all six terms → sum=3 → p+q=4. Mod 99991 ⇒ 4.

f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For odd n, smallest divisor d≥6 of n gives f=n−3d; d=n/p_min where p_min=smallest divisor≥6 of n not multiple of 3. For N=M+c (c≪M), N’s odd divisors≠3 are exactly odd divisors of c+1 (since M≡1 mod any odd d coprime 3). So p_min=smallest odd divisor≥6 of c+1 not divisible by 3. Then g(c)=(p_min−3)/p_min. Compute:
c=0,4M →p_min=9 →g=2/3.
c+1:1848375→p_min=25→g=22/25.
10162575→p_min=25→g=22/25.
265710645→p_min=97→g=94/97.
44636595→p_min=103→g=100/103.
Sum=3771562/749325 →(p+q) mod 99991=21292. Pitfall: include powers of 3 (9) for M, ignore 3‑divisible divisors.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b) with a+b=n‑1 ⇒ f(N)=S·(p‑1)/p where p=smallest divisor>2 of S=N‑1 (if S prime use 2S‑4). For M=3^K (K=2025!), 3^K≡1 mod d (d≤2025, d∤3). So p is smallest divisor>2 of c (or 4 if c≡0 mod4). Compute p: c=0→4; 4M→4; 1848374→11; 10162574→5081287 (since 3^K≡1 mod p and p|c); 265710644→4; 44636594→17. Then g(c)=α+⌊Kα·(c‑1)/M⌋/K; only c=0,4M give floor≠0 (‑1/K each). Sum= (3/4‑1/K)+(15/4‑1/K)+10/11+5081286/5081287+3/4+16/17. Reduce to p/q, compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfall: handle c=4M and prime‑case S.

f(N)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=N ⇒ f(N)=N·min_{d|N}L_d/d. Minimal ratios: 6/11 (d∈11ℕ), 4/7 (7ℕ), 16/25 (5²·ℕ), 64/97, 110/167. For N=M,5M ⇒2/3. Compute x=c+1, factor, pick smallest ratio divisor (odd,≠3). Sum:2/3+2/3+16/25+16/25+64/97+110/167=4776854/1214925 →p+q≡92310 (mod 99991).

For N=M+c (M=3^{2025!}) odd, f(N)=min{N( p‑3)/p , (2N‑4)/3} where p=smallest divisor ≥6 of N. Since N≡2 (mod 3) for all c≠0,4M, (2N‑4)/3< N(p‑3)/p (p>9). Thus g(c)=⌊2025!·(2/3)⌋/2025!=2/3 for every term. Sum=6·2/3=4 ⇒ p+q=5 ⇒ answer 5.
